title: Telecom store rep
tagline: Learn to match customers to the right phone and internet plans and close the sale on the floor.
setting: Conversations happen at a carrier store counter or demo table where walk-in shoppers browse devices and ask about plans.

scenarios.label: Walk in phone upgrade
scenarios.desc: A shopper with an aging phone wants a new device and a plan that fits their budget.
scenarios.setup: The shopper taps a flagship phone on the demo table and says, Just looking for something faster than my three year old model.
scenarios.objective: Recommend a phone and plan combo and schedule the activation today.
scenarios.moment: Saturday 11:15 am, bright morning light through the front glass

scenarios.label: Family plan switch
scenarios.desc: A parent compares multi line deals and wants to move four numbers from a rival carrier.
scenarios.setup: The shopper spreads a competitor bill on the counter and says, I have four lines and they keep raising the price.
scenarios.skills: Competitive comparison and port in coordination
scenarios.objective: Present a family plan offer, confirm port eligibility, and close the switch.
scenarios.moment: Tuesday 6:50 pm, golden hour glow on the demo wall

scenarios.label: Home internet bundle
scenarios.desc: A remote worker needs reliable home broadband and wants it bundled with their phone line.
scenarios.setup: The shopper opens a laptop showing speed test results and says, My video calls keep freezing, I need better home internet.
scenarios.objective: Qualify address for fiber or 5G home, build a phone plus internet bundle, and book the install.
scenarios.moment: Thursday 3:20 pm, overcast sky pressing against the windows

buyers.angle: Needs every fee explained before committing.
Wants the best specs fast, dislikes upsell.
Will walk away if the total monthly cost is not lower.
Needs clear port timeline for three employee lines.
Cannot tolerate install delays, will escalate fast.

objections: Your activation fee is higher than the store down the street
I don’t want insurance, why is it on the quote?
The competitor gives free phones for switching
My current contract ends in two months, I don’t want early termination fees
How do I know your 5G home internet actually reaches my apartment?
I’ve had billing mistakes before, how is this different?
Why does the unlimited plan throttle video at 480p?
If I bring my own phone, do I still pay the same monthly?

rubric.label: Needs discovery
rubric.what: Asks open questions about usage, budget, and pain points before recommending.

rubric.label: Plan matching
rubric.what: Connects the right plan tier and device to the shopper’s stated needs.

rubric.label: Port in clarity
rubric.what: Explains the number transfer steps, timeline, and any temporary service gaps.

rubric.label: Fee transparency
rubric.what: Itemises every recurring and one time charge so the total monthly cost is clear.

rubric.label: Compliance disclosure
rubric.what: States required regulatory disclosures, data caps, and arbitration clauses accurately.

rubric.label: Close and next steps
rubric.what: Confirms the deal, sets the activation or install date, and summarises what the shopper leaves with.

pitfalls: Quoting a promotional price without the qualifying auto pay or credit check conditions.
Activating a line before the port in completes, leaving the shopper without service.
Skipping the required arbitration clause and data management disclosures.
line: Selling phone and internet plans in a retail store

personas.name: Faye Karpov
personas.background: Faye moved to the city a year ago to work in tech support before switching to retail sales. She double checks every line item on a bill before signing up for a new plan.
pushbacks: The activation fee seems higher than the store down the street. Why is it priced like this?
Why is insurance automatically added to the quote? I don’t want it
Other carriers are offering free phones for switching, why should I stay with you?
wins_over: clear pricing with no hidden fees
demonstrating real coverage in her neighborhood
offering a flexible upgrade path without penalties

personas.name: Brian Patel
personas.background: Brian started as a technician at a hardware store before moving to retail tech sales. He knows the latest phones inside out and is focused on getting customers matched with what they need fast.
cares_about: getting the best specs for his budget
completing the sale in record time
pushbacks: Actually, the $50 activation fee covers remote setup we don’t get charged at other stores
Insurance protects you if something happens to the device, it’s not a scam, it’s standard coverage
Free phones often require long contracts and don’t include the plan you want

personas.name: Sofia Ramirez
personas.background: Sofia works full time as a retail telecom sales consultant. She raises two kids and carefully compares every monthly bill.
pushbacks: Your activation fee is higher than the store down the street
I don’t want insurance, why is it on the quote?
The competitor gives free phones for switching

personas.name: Ronald Knox
personas.background: Runs a local courier service with three drivers. He budgets tightly and plans ahead for phone costs. He’s done with wasted time and vague answers.
pushbacks: The activation fee is $50 here and $30 across the street, why charge more?
Why is insurance automatically on the quote? i don’t need it
Free phones from competitors? what’s the catch? i want the straight price
wins_over: i see you’ve already pulled up the port timeline for my team
you explained the 5g home setup matches my building’s signal
you didn’t push a plan i don’t need and listed all costs upfront

personas.name: Violet Chen
personas.background: Violet is a remote marketing manager juggling client meetings across time zones. She upgraded to wireless home internet to avoid unreliable service that stalled her work.
cares_about: no hidden fees on her bill
quick setup before her lease ends
pushbacks: Activation fees are too high compared to the store down the street; I need justification
Why is insurance automatically added? I don’t want it
Free phones from competitors are compelling, what extra value do you offer?
wins_over: showing a flexible contract ending when her current lease does
demonstrating 5G coverage reaching her building address
offering a technician who will install within 24 hours
